83:   const color = `#${(channels as number[]).map((part) => part.toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("")}`;

91: function cssFunctionArguments(value: string): string[] {
92:   const argumentsText = value.slice(value.indexOf("(") + 1, value.lastIndexOf(")"));
93:   const result: string[] = [];
94:   let start = 0;
95:   let depth = 0;
96:   let quote = "";
97:   let escaped = false;
98:   for (let index = 0; index < argumentsText.length; index += 1) {
99:     const character = argumentsText[index];
100:     if (quote) {
101:       if (escaped) escaped = false;
102:       else if (character === "\\") escaped = true;
103:       else if (character === quote) quote = "";
104:       continue;
105:     }
106:     if (character === '"' || character === "'") { quote = character; continue; }
107:     if (character === "(") { depth += 1; continue; }
108:     if (character === ")") { depth = Math.max(0, depth - 1); continue; }
109:     if (character === "," && depth === 0) {
110:       result.push(argumentsText.slice(start, index).trim());
111:       start = index + 1;
112:     }
113:   }
114:   result.push(argumentsText.slice(start).trim());
115:   return result.filter(Boolean);
116: }

118: interface GradientStop {
119:   color: string;
120:   opacity: number;
121:   offset?: number;
122: }
123: 
124: function gradientStop(value: string): GradientStop | undefined {
125:   const match = value.match(/^\s*(transparent|rgba?\([^)]*\)|#[\da-f]{3,8})(?:\s+(.+))?\s*$/i);
126:   const parsed = cssColorWithOpacity(match?.[1], true);
127:   if (!parsed) return undefined;
128:   // Percentages map directly to Penpot's normalized stop offsets. Pixel and
129:   // length-based positions depend on the rendered gradient line, which is
130:   // not available in the scene document, so retain CSS's interpolated offset
131:   // for those cases rather than inventing an incorrect absolute position.
132:   const percentage = match?.[2]?.match(/(?:^|\s)(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)%/);
133:   const offset = percentage ? clampOpacity(Number(percentage[1]) / 100) : undefined;
134:   return { ...parsed, offset };
135: }
136: 
137: function resolvedGradientOffsets(stops: GradientStop[]): number[] {
138:   const offsets = stops.map((stop) => stop.offset);
139:   if (offsets[0] === undefined) offsets[0] = 0;
140:   if (offsets[offsets.length - 1] === undefined) offsets[offsets.length - 1] = 1;
141:   // CSS's color-stop fixup first clamps every explicit stop against its
142:   // previous explicit/effective position. Only then are runs of omitted
143:   // positions interpolated, so an omitted stop never creates a backwards
144:   // segment that gets flattened after the fact.
145:   let previous = 0;
146:   for (let index = 0; index < offsets.length; index += 1) {
147:     if (offsets[index] !== undefined) {
148:       previous = Math.max(previous, clampOpacity(offsets[index] as number));
149:       offsets[index] = previous;
150:     }
151:   }
152:   for (let index = 0; index < offsets.length; index += 1) {
153:     if (offsets[index] !== undefined) continue;
154:     let next = index + 1;
155:     while (next < offsets.length && offsets[next] === undefined) next += 1;
156:     const start = offsets[index - 1] as number;
157:     const end = offsets[next] as number;
158:     const count = next - index + 1;
159:     for (let fill = index; fill < next; fill += 1) offsets[fill] = start + (end - start) * (fill - index + 1) / count;
160:     index = next;
161:   }
162:   return offsets as number[];
163: }

165: function gradientPrelude(type: "linear" | "radial", value: string | undefined): boolean {
166:   const source = value?.trim().toLowerCase() || "";
167:   if (type === "linear") {
168:     return /^(?:-?(?:\d+(?:\.\d*)?|\.\d+)deg|to\s+(?:(?:left|right)(?:\s+(?:top|bottom))?|(?:top|bottom)(?:\s+(?:left|right))?))$/.test(source);
169:   }
170:   // Keep the existing radial approximation for CSS's common geometry
171:   // preludes, including a position on its own and explicit radius lengths.
172:   // This deliberately recognizes geometry syntax only; a color hint or an
173:   // unsupported color function cannot take this path and be silently skipped.
174:   const number = "-?(?:\\d+(?:\\.\\d*)?|\\.\\d+)";
175:   const position = "(?:(?:left|center|right|top|bottom|" + number + "%)\\s*){1,2}";
176:   const length = number + "(?:px|em|rem|vw|vh|vmin|vmax|cm|mm|q|in|pt|pc)";
177:   const size = "(?:closest-side|closest-corner|farthest-side|farthest-corner|" + length + "(?:\\s+" + length + ")?)";
178:   return new RegExp("^(?:at\\s+" + position + "|(?:(?:circle|ellipse)(?:\\s+" + size + ")?|" + size + ")(?:\\s+at\\s+" + position + ")?)$").test(source);
179: }

181: function cssGradient(value: string | undefined): Gradient | undefined {
182:   const normalized = value?.trim().toLowerCase();
183:   const type = normalized?.startsWith("linear-gradient") ? "linear" : normalized?.startsWith("radial-gradient") ? "radial" : undefined;
184:   if (!type) return undefined;
185:   const source = value as string;
186:   const parts = cssFunctionArguments(source);
187:   // The optional first item is a direction/shape. Every remaining item must
188:   // be understood: filtering failed stops would silently change a gradient's
189:   // colors and stop interpolation.
190:   const stopParts = gradientStop(parts[0]) ? parts : gradientPrelude(type, parts[0]) ? parts.slice(1) : [];
191:   const parsedStops = stopParts.map(gradientStop);
192:   if (parsedStops.length < 2 || parsedStops.some((stop) => !stop)) return undefined;
193:   const colors = parsedStops as GradientStop[];
194:   const offsets = resolvedGradientOffsets(colors);
195:   const stops = colors.map(({ color, opacity }, index) => ({ color, opacity, offset: offsets[index] }));
196:   if (type === "radial") return { type: "radial", startX: 0.5, startY: 0.5, endX: 1, endY: 0.5, width: 0.5, stops };
197:   const angle = source.match(/(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)deg/);
198:   const degrees = angle ? Number(angle[1]) : 180;
199:   const radians = (degrees - 90) * Math.PI / 180;
200:   return { type: "linear", startX: 0.5 - Math.cos(radians) / 2, startY: 0.5 - Math.sin(radians) / 2, endX: 0.5 + Math.cos(radians) / 2, endY: 0.5 + Math.sin(radians) / 2, width: 1, stops };
201: }

203: function applyShadow(shape: Shape, value: string | undefined): void {
204:   if (!value || value === "none") return;
205:   const color = cssColorWithOpacity((value.match(/rgba?\([^)]*\)|#[\da-f]{3,8}/i) || [])[0]);
206:   const dimensions = (value.match(/-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?px/g) || []).map((dimension) => Number.parseFloat(dimension));
207:   if (!color || dimensions.length < 3) return;
208:   shape.shadows = [{ style: value.includes("inset") ? "inner-shadow" : "drop-shadow", offsetX: dimensions[0], offsetY: dimensions[1], blur: dimensions[2], spread: dimensions[3] || 0, color: { color: color.color, opacity: color.opacity } }];

216: function applyPaint(shape: Shape, paint: ScenePaint): void {
217:   const color = cssColorWithOpacity(paint.backgroundColor);
218:   const gradient = cssGradient(paint.backgroundImage);
219:   // CSS paints a background color before its image layers. Keep the element
220:   // opacity on the shape, otherwise a translucent color receives opacity
221:   // twice (once in its fill and once on its container).
222:   const fills: Fill[] = [
223:     ...(color ? [{ fillColor: color.color, fillOpacity: color.opacity }] : []),
224:     ...(gradient ? [{ fillColorGradient: gradient }] : [])
225:   ];
226:   if ("fills" in shape && shape.type !== "group") (shape as Shape & { fills: Fill[] }).fills = fills;
227:   shape.opacity = paint.opacity ?? 1;
228:   if (paint.radius) {
229:     [shape.borderRadiusTopLeft, shape.borderRadiusTopRight, shape.borderRadiusBottomRight, shape.borderRadiusBottomLeft] = paint.radius;
230:   }
231:   const stroke = cssColorWithOpacity(paint.borderColor);
232:   if (stroke && paint.borderWidth && paint.borderStyle !== "none") {
233:     shape.strokes = [{ strokeColor: stroke.color, strokeOpacity: stroke.opacity, strokeWidth: paint.borderWidth, strokeStyle: "solid", strokeAlignment: "center" }];
234:   }
235:   applyShadow(shape, paint.boxShadow);
236:   const matrix = paint.transform?.match(/^matrix\(([^)]+)\)$/);
237:   if (matrix) {
238:     const values = matrix[1].split(",").map(Number);
239:     if (values.length >= 2) shape.rotation = Math.atan2(values[1], values[0]) * 180 / Math.PI;
240:   }
241:   if (clipsContent(paint) && shape.type === "board") (shape as Board).clipContent = true;
242: }

279: function penpotFontFamily(value: string | undefined): string {

281:   return GENERIC_FONT_FAMILIES.has(family.toLowerCase()) ? "Inter" : family;

284: function penpotFontCandidates(value: string | undefined): string[] {
285:   const family = penpotFontFamily(value);
286:   if (family === "Inter") return [family];
287:   // Some webfont CSS declares the PostScript face name as the family, for
288:   // example `Poppins-Regular`. Penpot usually registers the family as
289:   // `Poppins`, so try that normalized name before falling back.
290:   const normalized = family.replace(/(?:[-_](?:regular|normal|italic|oblique|thin|extralight|light|medium|semibold|bold|extrabold|black)|[-_]\d{3})$/i, "");
291:   return normalized && normalized !== family ? [family, normalized, "Inter"] : [family, "Inter"];

294: function applyPenpotFontFamily(text: Text, value: string | undefined): void {

299:     } catch {

301:       // normalized family and finally the guaranteed Inter fallback.

310: function applyTextSizing(text: Text, style: NonNullable<SceneNode["textStyle"]>, scale: number): void {
311:   const baseFontSize = Math.max(1, style.fontSize);
312:   const effectiveScale = Math.max(0.01, scale);
313:   text.fontSize = String(Math.max(1, baseFontSize * effectiveScale));
314:   // Scene text styles use Penpot's unitless line-height multiplier. Scale
315:   // the multiplier inversely so reducing width does not collapse the source
316:   // line box vertically.
317:   text.lineHeight = String(Math.max(0.01, style.lineHeight / effectiveScale));
318:   // CSS permits negative tracking; Penpot's text API currently does not.
319:   text.letterSpacing = String(Math.max(0, style.letterSpacing * effectiveScale));
320: }

322: function createText(node: SceneNode): Text {
323:   const text = penpot.createText(node.text || "");
324:   if (!text) throw new Error(`Unable to create text layer: ${node.name}`);
325:   const style = node.textStyle;
326:   text.growType = "fixed";
327:   // CSS lays inline content out from the top of its line box. Make that
328:   // explicit because a Penpot text layer's editor default can be center.
329:   text.verticalAlign = "top";
330:   text.direction = "ltr";
331:   text.characters = node.text || "";
332:   if (style) {
333:     // CSS generic families (for example `system-ui`) are valid in a browser
334:     // but rejected by Penpot's fontFamily validator. Inter is Penpot's
335:     // guaranteed fallback and keeps the layer editable instead of aborting
336:     // the entire import.
337:     applyPenpotFontFamily(text, style.fontFamily);
338:     // Penpot's plugin API expects numeric string values, not CSS units.
339:     applyTextSizing(text, style, textFitScale(node));
340:     text.fontWeight = String(style.fontWeight);
341:     text.fontStyle = style.fontStyle === "italic" ? "italic" : "normal";
342:     // Captured line coordinates already include browser alignment offsets.
343:     text.align = node.textNoWrap ? "left" : textAlign(style.textAlign);
344:     const textTransform = ["uppercase", "lowercase", "capitalize"].find((value) => value === style.textTransform);

346:     if (style.textDecoration.includes("line-through")) text.textDecoration = "line-through";
347:     else if (style.textDecoration.includes("underline")) text.textDecoration = "underline";
348:   }
349:   const color = cssColorWithOpacity(node.paint.color, true);
350:   if (color) text.fills = [{ fillColor: color.color, fillOpacity: color.opacity }];
351:   text.opacity = node.paint.opacity ?? 1;
352:   return text;
353: }

355: function constrainTextToCapturedWidth(text: Text, node: SceneNode, maximum: number): void {

358:   const scale = Number(text.fontSize) / Math.max(1, node.textStyle.fontSize) * (maximum - 0.5) / actual;

362: async function mediaFor(asset: AssetRef) {
363:   const dataUrl = asset.dataUrl || (asset.url?.startsWith("data:") ? asset.url : undefined);
364:   if (dataUrl) {
365:     const response = await fetch(dataUrl);
366:     const data = new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer());
367:     return penpot.uploadMediaData(asset.id, data, response.headers.get("content-type") || asset.mimeType || "image/png");
368:   }
369:   if (asset.url) return penpot.uploadMediaUrl(asset.id, asset.url);
370:   return undefined;
371: }

377: function svgTextOf(asset: AssetRef | undefined): string | undefined {
378:   const url = asset?.dataUrl || asset?.url;
379:   if (!url || !url.toLowerCase().startsWith("data:image/svg+xml")) return undefined;
380:   const comma = url.indexOf(",");
381:   if (comma < 0) return undefined;
382:   const encoded = url.slice(comma + 1);
383:   if (url.slice(0, comma).toLowerCase().endsWith(";base64")) {
384:     try {
385:       const binary = atob(encoded);
386:       const bytes = Uint8Array.from(binary, (character) => character.charCodeAt(0));
387:       if (typeof TextDecoder === "function") {
388:         try { return new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: false }).decode(bytes).trim(); } catch { /* Use the binary fallback below. */ }
389:       }
390:       return binary;
391:     } catch { return undefined; }
392:   }
393:   try {
394:     const svg = decodeURIComponent(encoded).trim();
395:     return /<svg[\s>]/i.test(svg) ? svg : undefined;
396:   } catch { return undefined; }
397: }

405:     (paint.boxShadow && paint.boxShadow !== "none") ||

413: async function applyAssetFill(shape: Shape, asset: AssetRef | undefined, media: MediaCache): Promise<boolean> {
414:   if (!asset || shape.type === "group") return false;
415:   const key = mediaKey(asset);
416:   let uploaded = media.has(key) ? media.get(key) || undefined : undefined;
417:   if (!media.has(key)) {
418:     try {
419:       uploaded = await mediaFor(asset);
420:       media.set(key, uploaded || null);
421:     } catch {
422:       // Cache failures as well as successes so repeated responsive boards do
423:       // not retry an unavailable asset for every viewport.
424:       media.set(key, null);
425:       return false;
426:     }
427:   }
428:   if (!uploaded) return false;
429:   const fillTarget = shape as Shape & { fills: Fill[] };
430:   fillTarget.fills = [...(fillTarget.fills || []), { fillImage: uploaded, fillOpacity: 1 }];
431:   return true;
432: }

476: async function createShape(node: SceneNode, assets: Map<string, AssetRef>, media: MediaCache): Promise<Shape> {

518:   // Re-uploading the same page asset for each viewport creates noisy failed
519:   // requests in Penpot and needlessly increases the file update payload.
520:   const media: MediaCache = new Map();

522:   try {
523:     for (const scene of scenes) {
524:       if (options.isCancelled()) throw new ImportCancelledError();

543:           siblings.push(node);

28: type BaselineMetadata = {
29:   inputs: { extractor: { path: string; sha256: string }; assets: Array<{ path: string; sha256: string }> };
30:   fixtures: Array<{ file: string; sha256: string }>;
31: };
32: type BaselineSceneEvidence = {
33:   fixtures: Array<{ file: string; sha256: string; viewports: Array<{ scene: SceneDocument }> }>;
34: };
35: 
36: function fixturePath(path: string): string {
37:   return resolve(process.cwd(), "src", "capture", "fixtures", path);
38: }
39: 
40: function sha256File(path: string): string {
41:   return createHash("sha256").update(readFileSync(path)).digest("hex");
42: }
43: 
44: function baselineEvidence(): { metadata: BaselineMetadata; scenes: BaselineSceneEvidence } {
45:   return {
46:     metadata: JSON.parse(readFileSync(fixturePath("baselines/metadata.json"), "utf8")) as BaselineMetadata,
47:     scenes: JSON.parse(readFileSync(fixturePath("baselines/scene-evidence.json"), "utf8")) as BaselineSceneEvidence
48:   };
49: }
50: 
51: function scenesForFixture(evidence: BaselineSceneEvidence, file: string): SceneDocument[] {
52:   const fixture = evidence.fixtures.find((candidate) => candidate.file === file);
53:   if (!fixture) throw new Error(`Missing generated scene evidence for ${file}.`);
54:   return fixture.viewports.map(({ scene }) => scene);
55: }
56: 
57: function shapesBelow(shape: FakeShape, seen = new Set<FakeShape>()): FakeShape[] {
58:   if (seen.has(shape)) return [];
59:   seen.add(shape);
60:   return [shape, ...(shape.children || []).flatMap((child) => shapesBelow(child, seen))];
61: }

63: function scene(name = "Desktop"): SceneDocument {
64:   return {
65:     protocolVersion: PROTOCOL_VERSION,
66:     viewport: { id: name.toLowerCase(), name, width: 400, height: 300 },
67:     documentSize: { width: 400, height: 300 },
68:     assets: [],
69:     diagnostics: [],
70:     nodes: [{ id: "root", children: ["text"], kind: "container", name: "body", source: "body", rect: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 400, height: 300 }, zIndex: 1, paint: { backgroundColor: "rgb(255, 255, 255)" }, layout: { kind: "flex", direction: "column" } }, { id: "text", parentId: "root", children: [], kind: "text", name: "Hello", source: "body ::text", rect: { x: 20, y: 20, width: 80, height: 24 }, zIndex: 2, paint: { color: "rgb(0, 0, 0)" }, layout: { kind: "none" }, text: "Hello", textStyle: { fontFamily: "Inter", fontSize: 16, fontWeight: 400, fontStyle: "normal", lineHeight: 1.5, letterSpacing: 0, textAlign: "left", textDecoration: "none", textTransform: "none" } }]

+# HTML importer upgrade plan
+
+Status: in progress.
+
+## Objective
+
+Improve visual fidelity and predictable imports first, then improve performance and native Penpot editability. Preserve the separation between browser capture, the scene document, and Penpot object creation.
+
+This plan follows a code review of `src/capture`, `src/importer/penpot.ts`, the scene contracts and validation, and the plugin/UI lifecycle. The baseline suite passes: 124 tests across 14 files. The findings are code-based; live browser and Penpot validation remains to be done.
+
+## Phase 1 — Regression fixtures and visual baseline
+
+- [ ] Add browser-based extraction tests that execute the sandbox and inspect the resulting scene, supplementing the existing generated-script string checks.
+- [ ] Create small HTML fixtures for background images, nested clipping, alpha/opacity, stacking, `display: contents`, whitespace, and failed assets.
+- [ ] Use bundled assets and fonts for deterministic fixtures; keep network-failure cases separate.
+- [ ] Capture reference screenshots at desktop, tablet, and mobile widths.
+- [ ] Document a repeatable live Penpot comparison workflow, including host version, font availability, and expected layer structure.
+- [ ] Add regression coverage with each fix below; avoid requiring all future fixtures before starting implementation.
+
+Acceptance: each fidelity change has a focused behavioral test and a reproducible visual comparison. Tests validate output, not merely the presence of implementation strings.
+
+## Phase 2 — Highest-impact fidelity fixes
+
+### 2.1 Container and root background images
+
+Relevant code: `createShape()`, `createContainerBackdrop()`, and root rendering in `src/importer/penpot.ts`.
+
+- [x] Share asset-fill resolution between ordinary shapes, container backdrops, and root boards.
+- [x] Preserve background color beneath image fills where supported.
+- [ ] Extend the scene contract to capture background size, position, and repeat when needed for correct placement.
+- [ ] Define handling for multiple background layers; report unsupported combinations explicitly.
+- [ ] Test a hero image behind a heading, a body background, and reuse of the same asset across viewports.
+
+Acceptance: adding child content to an element does not cause its background image to disappear; supported background placement matches the fixture.
+
+### 2.2 Nested overflow clipping
+
+Relevant code: `applyPaint()` and the container branch of `render()` in `src/importer/penpot.ts`.
+
+- [ ] Verify available clipping and masking behavior in the installed Penpot API and live host.
+- [ ] Use a clipping-capable container where CSS requires clipping, while retaining simple groups elsewhere. (Deferred: the initial `Group.makeMask()` implementation hid content in live Penpot mobile output; verify mask ordering and coordinate behavior before retrying.)
+- [ ] Preserve source bounds independently of descendant bounds and keep child coordinates correct.
+- [ ] Capture overflow axes separately; define and diagnose combinations that cannot be reproduced.
+- [ ] Test oversized children, rounded cards, nested clips, and visible overflow.
+
+Acceptance: content stays within the intended clip, including supported rounded corners, without shifting descendants.
+
+### 2.3 Color alpha and element opacity

+### 2.3 Color alpha and element opacity
+
+Relevant code: `cssColor()`, `cssGradient()`, `applyPaint()`, `createText()`, and `appendText()`.
+
+- [x] Represent color and alpha separately for fills, strokes, shadows, and gradient stops.
+- [x] Apply CSS element opacity once to the appropriate shape or compositing container.
+- [x] Remove duplicated parent opacity from synthetic direct-text children.
+- [ ] Preserve gradient stop positions and alpha for supported gradients.
+- [ ] Define normalization or diagnostics for color formats outside the supported parser.
+- [ ] Test translucent backgrounds, shadows, nested opacity, and decorated text at 50% opacity.
+
+Acceptance: color alpha and element opacity combine correctly; a solid element with `opacity: .5` is not unintentionally reduced to .25.
+
+## Phase 3 — Capture correctness and paint order
+
+### 3.1 Visible descendants
+
+- [x] Separate whether an element produces a scene node from whether its descendants should be visited.
+- [x] Traverse `display: contents` and zero-sized wrappers with visible descendants.
+- [x] Preserve subtree suppression for `display: none` and fully transparent compositing groups.
+- [x] Handle descendants that override an ancestor's `visibility: hidden`.
+- [ ] Assign children to the correct surviving scene ancestor when a wrapper has no node.
+
+Acceptance: visible descendants survive wrapper omission, and hidden subtrees remain absent.
+
+### 3.2 Stacking order
+
+- [ ] Preserve `z-index: auto` separately from numeric zero; avoid substituting traversal sequence for explicit zero.
+- [ ] Capture enough stacking-context information to reproduce supported CSS paint order.
+- [ ] Order siblings and context contents with stable source-order tie breaking.
+- [ ] Verify that Penpot grouping preserves the intended backdrop and child order.
+- [ ] Test negative, zero, and positive z-index; positioned overlaps; and nested contexts caused by opacity or transforms.
+
+Acceptance: overlap fixtures match browser paint order without globally sorting unrelated stacking contexts.
+
+### 3.3 Text whitespace and placement
+
+- [ ] Respect computed `white-space` rather than compacting all text unconditionally.
+- [ ] Preserve meaningful spaces across inline element boundaries, nonbreaking spaces, preformatted indentation, and explicit line breaks.
+- [ ] Capture all direct text nodes, including text separated by comments or other non-rendered nodes.
+- [ ] Use measured text bounds consistently for single-line and multiline content.
+- [ ] Add fixtures for mixed formatting, centered text, padded text, code blocks, and font fallback.
+- [ ] Define whether line-preserving text remains the default and document its editing tradeoff.
+
+Acceptance: fixture text retains its content, spacing, and line placement without missing runs or accidental reflow.
+
+## Phase 4 — Reliable assets and import lifecycle
+
+### 4.1 Asset failures and diagnostics
+
+- [ ] Cache both successful and failed asset resolutions across responsive boards.
+- [ ] Render a visible, named placeholder when an image cannot be imported.
+- [ ] Return import-time diagnostics to the UI, including asset source and failure reason.
+- [ ] Distinguish editable SVG success, raster fallback, and complete failure.
+- [ ] Test a repeated failing URL and cancellation during an asset operation.
+
+Acceptance: one failing shared asset does not trigger repeated uploads, silently disappear, or prevent unrelated layers from importing.
+
+### 4.2 Scene validation and workload limits
+
+- [ ] Validate paint, text styles, layouts, asset fields, and diagnostics before host mutation.

content.text:
Phase 3.1 is done — both remaining items are checked off in the plan.

**What I found**
- Surviving-ancestor parenting already worked: I probed zero-size wrappers, `visibility: hidden` with a revived child, and nested `display: contents` — text, elements, and DOM order all land on the correct surviving node, hidden text stays absent. What was missing was locked-in regression coverage, so I added it rather than changing behavior.
- The wrapper-collapse rename was a real bug in `src/importer/penpot.ts`: an undecorated single-child container reused its child's shape, then overwrote the child's name/source with the wrapper's. Notably, the checked-in `color-opacity` scene had this live — the nested-opacity text layer was named `#nested-opacity` instead of its own source.

**Changes**
- `src/importer/penpot.ts` — collapsed wrappers (single child, no backdrop) now keep the child's name/source/plugin data; only the wrapper's compositing opacity still multiplies on.
- `src/importer/penpot.test.ts` — new test: wrapper collapsing onto a clipping board keeps the clip's identity with wrapper opacity applied; updated the generated opacity-scene test to assert the surviving child source, 0.25 opacity, and no `#nested-opacity` rename trace.
- `src/capture/extractor.test.ts` — new test: omitted-wrapper children parent to the surviving scene ancestor in DOM order, hidden-wrapper text stays absent.
- `IMPORTER-UPGRADE-PLAN.md` — both 3.1 boxes checked, with a reference-evidence note.

**Verification:** focused suite 70/70 pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Remaining in Phase 3: **3.2 stacking order** (I confirmed `z-index: auto` vs `0` both fall through to traversal sequence — the fixture shows `auto`→11, `zero`→13) and **3.3 text whitespace** (fixture shows leading spaces/tabs compacted). Say the word when you want the next slice.

## Text capture policy

Line-preserving text remains the default: every source line becomes its own
non-wrapping text layer at its measured position, so the import matches the
browser even when the Penpot host substitutes wider fallback fonts. The
tradeoff is editability: editing one line never reflows its neighbors, and
the layer tree has one layer per line instead of one per paragraph. This is
the snapshot-importer contract, not a layout conversion; native reflowing
text belongs to the Phase 6 layout milestone.

Per-line layers carry measured bounds (`textMaxWidth`, `textFitScale`) so an
overflowing fallback font shrinks toward its source width instead of painting
over neighboring content. Runs longer than 20,000 characters skip
per-character measurement and import as a single collapsed layer.

1: #!/usr/bin/env node
2: /** Serve deterministic importer fixtures with CORS for a live Penpot pass. */
3: import { createServer } from "node:http";
4: import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
5: import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
6: import { dirname, extname, resolve, sep } from "node:path";
7: 
8: const root = resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "src", "capture", "fixtures");
9: const port = Number(process.env.IMPORTER_FIXTURE_PORT || 4174);
10: const mimeTypes = { ".html": "text/html; charset=utf-8", ".svg": "image/svg+xml", ".ttf": "font/ttf", ".woff": "font/woff", ".woff2": "font/woff2" };
11: 
12: const server = createServer(async (request, response) => {
13:   let pathname;
14:   try {
15:     pathname = decodeURIComponent(new URL(request.url || "/", "http://fixture.local").pathname);
16:   } catch {
17:     response.writeHead(400, { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*", "Cache-Control": "no-store" });
18:     response.end("Malformed fixture URL");
19:     return;
20:   }
21:   const target = resolve(root, `.${pathname}`);
22:   const commonHeaders = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*", "Cache-Control": "no-store" };
23:   if (pathname === "/favicon.ico") {
24:     response.writeHead(204, commonHeaders);
25:     response.end();
26:     return;
27:   }
28:   if (!(target.startsWith(`${root}${sep}`))) {
29:     response.writeHead(403, commonHeaders);
30:     response.end("Outside fixture root");
31:     return;
32:   }
33:   try {
34:     const bytes = await readFile(target);
35:     response.writeHead(200, { ...commonHeaders, "Content-Type": mimeTypes[extname(target).toLowerCase()] || "application/octet-stream" });
36:     response.end(bytes);
37:   } catch {
38:     // asset-failures.html intentionally uses this branch for one local URL.
39:     response.writeHead(404, { ...commonHeaders, "Content-Type": "text/plain; charset=utf-8" });
40:     response.end("Fixture asset intentionally absent");
41:   }
42: });
43: 
44: server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
45:   process.stdout.write(`Importer fixtures: http://127.0.0.1:${port}/background-images.html\n`);
46: });

Here's how to test the Phase 3 work in a browser with the example fixtures. You're on branch `fix/importer-visible-descendants`, so build from there.

## 1. Start the plugin

```sh
npm run dev
```

In Penpot's plugin manager, load the manifest URL Vite prints (per the README's WSL section: `http://localhost:4173/manifest.json` from Windows, or the WSL IP under Vite's **Network** line if localhost forwarding is broken). Keep `npm run dev` running.

## 2. Serve the fixtures

In a second terminal:

```sh
npm run serve:importer-fixtures
```

This serves `http://127.0.0.1:4174/` — one page per fixture:

- `background-images.html`
- `overflow-clipping.html`
- `color-opacity.html`
- `stacking-contents-whitespace.html` (the Phase 3 one)
- `asset-failures.html`

## 3. Import each fixture

For each page: open its URL in your browser, copy the full HTML source, paste it into the plugin, and set the plugin's **Base URL** to the exact served page (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:4174/stacking-contents-whitespace.html`). The Base URL step is required — without it, relative images/fonts won't resolve. Import all three viewport boards (Desktop 1440×900, Tablet 768×1024, Mobile 390×844).

## 4. What to check per fixture

Compare each board against its checked-in reference screenshot in `src/capture/fixtures/baselines/` at 100% zoom.

**Stacking / wrappers / whitespace** (`stacking-contents-whitespace.html` — the Phase 3 fixture):
- Overlap order is negative → auto → zero → positive, even though the HTML lists them positive-first. This is the test that fails without the fix.
- No `contents` wrapper layer exists, but `surviving child` is present.
- Code block keeps `  leading  spaces` indentation, tab-indented `        return true;`, NBSP line unbroken, mixed bold/italic/linked runs all present.

**Backgrounds**: hero image stays behind the heading, body background covers the board, repeated tile reuses one asset, color shows beneath images.

**Clipping**: `#outer-clip`/`#inner-clip` are nested clipping boards (not groups) that keep their own bounds; rounded cards keep corner radius; the single-axis case imports *unclipped* with an `UNSUPPORTED_OVERFLOW` diagnostic.

**Opacity**: nested opacity composites to .25 applied once (not squared); decorated text at .5 keeps its fill; transparent text doesn't turn black.

**Asset failures**: 3 boards, each with 3 placeholders named `Image unavailable: missing-image-a/b` and `missing-background`.

## 5. Layer tree + undo

Expect one board per viewport (`Page — Desktop 1440`, etc.). Clipping samples nest boards; everything else groups. Undo removes **one board per undo step** (3 undos for 3 boards), redo restores them, nothing residual left behind.

## 6. Notes

- **Fonts**: text fixtures use DejaVu Sans. If Penpot renders text wider/narrower than the screenshots, that's host font substitution — record whether DejaVu Sans regular/bold is actually installed on the Penpot host rather than treating it as an import bug.
- `asset-failures.html` intentionally 404s one local asset; every other fixture must load with zero failed requests.
- This matches the fuller record template in `docs/importer-visual-baselines.md` ("Live Penpot comparison procedure") if you want to log host version, commit, and mismatches per fixture.

Problem
appendChild() and insertChild() are only defined on Board and Boolean in the Plugin API. Attempting to call these methods on a Group, Rectangle, or other shape type throws: TypeError: shape.appendChild is not a function However, Penpot's internal data model supports arbitrary parent-child relationships between shapes. The restriction is in the Plugin API surface only.
Impact
Plugins cannot dynamically reparent shapes into groups
Shapes created outside a board cannot be moved inside a board without creating a new board
LLM-generated plugin code frequently attempts group.appendChild() based on logical assumptions

penpot-mcp #32: z-order is reversed when using appendChild
Proposed Fix
Extend appendChild/insertChild to Group and other container types that logically support children: export interface Group extends ShapeBase { children: Shape[]; appendChild(child: Shape): void; insertChild(index: number, child: Shape): void; }

* insertChild(3, D) gives a group with layers A, B, C, D

Remarks ​
This array can be read like and iterated like a regular array. However, calling this property always returns a new array, and both the property and the new array are read-only.

(defn interaction-proxy
  [plugin-id file-id page-id shape-id index]
  (obj/reify {:name "InteractionProxy"}
    :$plugin {:enumerable false :get (fn [] plugin-id)}
    :$file   {:enumerable false :get (fn [] file-id)}
    :$page   {:enumerable false :get (fn [] page-id)}
    :$shape  {:enumerable false :get (fn [] shape-id)}
    :$index  {:enumerable false :get (fn [] index)}

    ;; Not enumerable so we don't have an infinite loop
    :shape
    {:enumerable false
     :get (fn [] (shape-proxy plugin-id file-id page-id shape-id))}

    :trigger
    {:this true
     :get #(-> % u/proxy->interaction :event-type format/format-key)
     :set
     (fn [_ value]
       (let [value (parser/parse-keyword value)]
         (cond
           (not (contains? ctsi/event-types value))
           (u/not-valid plugin-id :trigger value)

           (not (r/check-permission plugin-id "content:write"))
           (u/not-valid plugin-id :trigger "Plugin doesn't have 'content:write' permission")

           :else
           (st/emit! (dwi/update-interaction
                      (u/locate-shape file-id page-id shape-id)
                      index
                      #(assoc % :event-type value)
                      {:page-id page-id})))))}

    :delay
    {:this true
     :get #(-> % u/proxy->interaction :delay)
     :set
     (fn [_ value]
       (cond
         (or (not (sm/valid-safe-int? value)) (neg? value))
         (u/not-valid plugin-id :delay value)

         (not (r/check-permission plugin-id "content:write"))
         (u/not-valid plugin-id :delay "Plugin doesn't have 'content:write' permission")

         :else
         (st/emit! (dwi/update-interaction
                    (u/locate-shape file-id page-id shape-id)
                    index
                    #(assoc % :delay value)
                    {:page-id page-id}))))}

    :action
    {:this true
     :get #(-> % u/proxy->interaction (format/format-action plugin-id file-id page-id))
     :set
     (fn [self value]
       (let [params (parser/parse-action value)
             interaction
             (-> (u/proxy->interaction self)
                 (d/patch-object params))]
         (cond
           (not (sm/validate ctsi/schema:interaction interaction))
           (u/not-valid plugin-id :action interaction)

           (not (r/check-permission plugin-id "content:write"))
           (u/not-valid plugin-id :action "Plugin doesn't have 'content:write' permission")

           :else
           (st/emit! (dwi/update-interaction
                      (u/locate-shape file-id page-id shape-id)
                      index
                      #(d/patch-object % params)
                      {:page-id page-id})))))}

    :remove
    (fn []
      (cond
        (not (r/check-permission plugin-id "content:write"))
        (u/not-valid plugin-id :remove "Plugin doesn't have 'content:write' permission")

        :else
        (st/emit! (dwi/remove-interaction {:id shape-id} index))))))

(defn- z-order-location
  "Map a plugin z-order intent (:top/:bottom/:up/:down) to the internal
  vertical-order location. Flex layouts store their children in reverse of the
  order the plugin exposes (see the `:children` getter), so front/back and
  forward/backward are inverted for a flex parent under natural child ordering."
  [plugin-id file-id page-id id loc]
  (let [shape     (u/locate-shape file-id page-id id)
        parent    (u/locate-shape file-id page-id (:parent-id shape))
        reversed? (and (u/natural-child-ordering? plugin-id)
                       (ctl/flex-layout? parent))]
    (if reversed?
      (case loc :top :bottom :bottom :top :up :down :down :up)
      loc)))

           ;; Methods
           :resize
           (fn [width height]
             (cond
               (or (not (sm/valid-safe-number? width)) (<= width 0))
               (u/not-valid plugin-id :resize width)

               (or (not (sm/valid-safe-number? height)) (<= height 0))
               (u/not-valid plugin-id :resize height)

               (not (r/check-permission plugin-id "content:write"))
               (u/not-valid plugin-id :resize "Plugin doesn't have 'content:write' permission")

               (not (u/page-active? page-id))
               (u/not-valid plugin-id :resize "Cannot modify a page that is not currently active")

               :else
               ;; A layout container that hugs its content (or a hugging/filling
               ;; layout child) ignores explicit dimensions and snaps back, so
               ;; switch the non-fixed axes to fixed sizing first, mirroring an
               ;; interactive drag resize. The sizing change must commit before
               ;; the resize, otherwise the layout reflows the new size away.
               (let [shape   (u/locate-shape file-id page-id id)
                     objects (u/locate-objects file-id page-id)
                     layout? (or (ctl/any-layout-immediate-child? objects shape)
                                 (ctl/any-layout? shape))
                     sizing  (cond-> {}
                               (and layout? (not= (:layout-item-h-sizing shape) :fix))
                               (assoc :layout-item-h-sizing :fix)

                               (and layout? (not= (:layout-item-v-sizing shape) :fix))
                               (assoc :layout-item-v-sizing :fix))]
                 (apply st/emit!
                        (cond-> []
                          (seq sizing)
                          (conj (dwsl/update-layout #{id} sizing))

                          :always
                          (conj (dw/update-dimensions [id] :width width)
                                (dw/update-dimensions [id] :height height)))))))

content.text:
You're right, and good catch — the stacking card is exactly upside-down: purple (negative) on top, red (positive) buried. Everything else in your screenshot looks correct (whitespace, display:contents, code block all good).

**Root cause:** my sort order was right, but I had Penpot's append direction backwards. I verified against Penpot's actual source (`frontend/src/app/plugins/shape.cljs` in penpot/penpot): under default plugin flags, `appendChild` inserts each child at **index 0, behind** existing children — not on top. So my bottom-first appends produced inverted stacking live. (This also matches two known upstream reports: "z-order is reversed when using appendChild" and appendChild "inserts at unpredictable position".)

**Fix committed as `902355d` on the branch:**
- Siblings now append **topmost-first**, so live shapes land back-to-front in browser paint order.
- Group members run back-to-front with the backdrop behind (layer texts stay visible, as in your screenshot).
- Capture side (`zIndexAuto`, `positioned`) was already correct — untouched.
- Full suite 173/173 + typecheck clean.

To re-test: pull the branch, `npm run dev` (rebuild), delete the old boards, and re-import `stacking-contents-whitespace.html`. Expected: red (positive) fully on top with its label visible, then yellow (auto), green (zero), purple (negative) behind everything.

One honest caveat: I reasoned out the group-member direction from your screenshot (texts visible ⇒ backdrop behind text) rather than from source, so when you re-check, please confirm each layer's label still renders above its own background. If anything still looks off, send another screenshot and the layer-panel order and I'll dig further.
